title: Scaffold the Go and Vue monorepo build
summary: Create the minimal buildable repository structure and shared developer commands without implementing product features.
objective: Give later backend and frontend tasks a deterministic Go module, Vue TypeScript workspace, embedded-asset boundary, and common verification entrypoints.
context: The accepted plan uses one Go executable serving an embedded Vue PWA. Parallel work must start from a stable repository layout and repeatable commands.
outputs: Initialized Go module and empty composition-root package
Vue 3 + TypeScript + Vite PWA workspace under web/
A declared generated-asset location that Go can embed after the frontend build
Documented repository-level commands for format, lint, test, frontend build, and Go build
implementation_notes: Keep the initial Go domain/application packages free of infrastructure dependencies.
Pin toolchain and package versions through normal lock/module files.
Do not add a production framework or dependency without using it for an accepted requirement.
A development fallback may serve frontend assets from disk, but the release boundary must support embedding compiled assets.
acceptance_criteria: A clean checkout can install frontend dependencies, build the Vue application, and build the Go command using documented commands.
The Go build has an explicit location from which compiled frontend assets will be embedded without committing build output.
Repository ignore rules exclude local SQLite files, secret material, downloaded content, frontend dependencies, generated build output, and caches.
No product feature, remote service, account system, or task-backlog change is introduced.
verification: Run Go formatting and `go test ./...`.
Run frontend lint/typecheck if configured and the production frontend build.
Run the documented Go build after producing frontend assets.
Inspect `git status --short` to confirm runtime/build artifacts remain untracked or ignored.
proof_required: Command transcript for clean Go and frontend builds
Changed-file inventory showing only scaffold/configuration paths
edge_cases: Frontend assets have not yet been built.
Commands run from a path containing spaces on Windows.
No C compiler is installed on the build machine.
non_goals: Creating an installer or background service
handoff_notes: Publish the final directory map and exact verification commands before dependent contract work begins.

title: Define domain entities and application ports
summary: Create dependency-free Go types and interfaces for profiles, sources, articles, library state, refresh runs, ranking configuration, repositories, and external adapters.
objective: Freeze the core vocabulary and dependency direction consumed by persistence, ingestion, ranking, HTTP, and frontend-contract work.
context: The planning package requires ports for persistence, fetching, credentials, clocks, ingestion adapters, and ranking while keeping domain rules independent of infrastructure.
outputs: Go domain types with validation-oriented value objects
Feed/API/scraper adapter, HTTP fetcher, credential store, and clock port interfaces
Typed application commands, queries, result types, and sentinel/domain errors
implementation_notes: Represent optional demographics explicitly; absence and disabled state must not collapse into a guessed value.
Represent content permission independently from whether content text happens to be present.
Keep secrets write-only at the application boundary: use credential identifiers, not secret-bearing domain records.
Define score contributions as machine-readable values from which the API can render explanations without recomputing rank logic.
acceptance_criteria: Domain packages import no SQLite, HTTP framework, browser, Windows credential, or source-specific adapter packages.
The interfaces cover profile/source configuration, refresh, article persistence, library actions, ranking configuration/results, and credential references.
Content permission, scraper policy state, refresh partial failures, optional demographic controls, and ranking explanation components are represented explicitly.
Compile-time interface tests or focused unit tests demonstrate intended dependency inversion.
verification: Run `go test ./internal/domain/... ./internal/application/...`.
Run a dependency/import check proving domain packages do not import infrastructure adapters.
Review public types against every entity and service in `assembly/generated/project_spec.json`.
proof_required: A concise port inventory for downstream implementers
edge_cases: Duplicate canonical URLs from different fetches
Optional demographics present but individually disabled
One source failing within an otherwise successful refresh
non_goals: Final ranking formulas or default weights
handoff_notes: Any later domain-contract change requires coordination with both implementation lanes and regenerated API fixtures where affected.

title: Specify the versioned local HTTP API
summary: Replace the placeholder API description with the canonical OpenAPI contract for setup, profile, sources, credentials, refresh, feed, article detail, library state, and ranking settings.
objective: Let frontend and backend work independently against one reviewed request/response and error contract.
context: The API is local and loopback-only, but still needs stable validation, pagination, errors, refresh progress, permission states, and explanation shapes.
inputs: Domain commands, queries, errors, and explanation types from CONTRACT-002
Frontend screens and backend services from assembly/generated/project_spec.json
outputs: Documented generation/check command for TypeScript bindings
Representative request, response, and error fixtures
Contract rules for pagination, timestamps, identifiers, optional fields, and credential write/delete behavior
implementation_notes: Use a versioned `/api/v1` prefix.
Never expose a credential read endpoint or return secret values after writes.
Make full-content permission and publisher-link fallback explicit in article responses.
Return score components and stable reason codes; presentation strings may be formed by the frontend without re-ranking.
acceptance_criteria: The contract covers every accepted MVP screen and operation without exposing postponed features.
Mutations define validation errors and conflict/not-found behavior; list operations define stable cursor or page semantics.
Refresh start and status responses represent running, partial-success, success, and failure outcomes.
Credential responses reveal only configured/not-configured state and never secret values.
A deterministic command regenerates TypeScript bindings and a drift check fails when generated files differ.
verification: Validate api/openapi.yaml with the selected OpenAPI validator.
Run the TypeScript client/type generator and its clean-tree drift check.
Compile representative Go handler interfaces and frontend fixture consumers against the contract.
Search response fixtures for secret-like values and prohibited full-content cases.
edge_cases: Empty feed and final pagination page
Concurrent refresh request while one is running
Metadata-only articles that still contain an excerpt
handoff_notes: Frontend and backend tasks must consume this contract; incompatible changes require coordinated versioning rather than silent drift.

title: Design the initial SQLite migration set
summary: Define ordered, restart-safe migrations for all authoritative MVP data while excluding secrets and disposable browser state.
objective: Provide a reviewed persistence contract before repositories, ingestion, and ranking implementations begin.
context: SQLite stores profile, sources, article metadata/permitted content, library state, refresh history, token/index data, and ranking results. Windows Credential Manager stores secret values.
inputs: Domain entities and repository ports from CONTRACT-002
Persistence and credential boundaries in merged requirements
outputs: Schema constraints and indexes for source identity, article deduplication, feed queries, and refresh history
Migration runner contract including application schema version behavior
implementation_notes: Prefer pure-Go SQLite compatibility unless a later accepted decision explicitly permits CGO.
Store credential reference identifiers and configured state only.
Retain raw fetched payloads only if a later task proves they are required and permitted; they are not part of this initial schema.
Choose stable time and boolean representations and document them.
acceptance_criteria: Applying all migrations to an empty database creates every required MVP table, constraint, and index.
Re-running the migration command is safe and reports the current schema version.
The schema enforces stable article deduplication and valid source/library relationships.
No table or column stores API secret values, inferred demographic data, or unpermitted full content.
The design supports transactional refresh writes and ranked-feed query patterns.
verification: Apply migrations to a temporary empty SQLite database.
Re-run migrations and assert idempotent version behavior.
Exercise foreign-key and unique-constraint failure fixtures.
Inspect the schema for forbidden credential-value columns.
proof_required: Migration test output against a temporary database
Schema inventory with indexes and invariants
edge_cases: Legacy database with an unknown newer schema version
Two source URLs resolving to the same canonical article URL
Nullable optional demographic and article metadata fields
handoff_notes: Persistence implementations must use these migrations as the only schema authority and add future changes through new migration files.

title: Build the loopback application host
summary: Implement the Go composition root that starts a loopback-only HTTP server, serves embedded frontend assets, opens the default browser after readiness, and shuts down cleanly.
objective: Provide the secure local runtime boundary required by every backend endpoint and the single-executable Windows experience.
context: The app is manually launched, has no authentication, and therefore must not listen on non-loopback interfaces by default.
implementation_notes: Bind explicitly to 127.0.0.1 or ::1 and use an available configured/default port without falling back to all interfaces.
Open the browser only after a readiness probe succeeds.
Use structured logs that exclude request bodies, credentials, and article content.
Make browser launching injectable so tests do not open a real browser.
acceptance_criteria: The process serves `/api/v1` and embedded SPA assets only on loopback by default.
Direct navigation to a client-side route returns the SPA entrypoint without shadowing API 404 responses.
Browser launch occurs once after readiness and a launch failure does not terminate the server.
Interrupt or termination signals trigger bounded graceful shutdown with deterministic exit behavior.
Startup errors are actionable and sanitized.
verification: Run Go unit tests with injected listener, clock, and browser launcher.
Run an integration test that asserts the bound address is loopback.
Test SPA fallback, API 404 isolation, readiness ordering, and graceful shutdown.
Build the command for Windows.
proof_required: Windows cross-build or native build output
edge_cases: Missing embedded build assets in development
handoff_notes: Expose a small composition interface so persistence and application services can be wired without putting business rules in main.

title: Create deterministic cross-layer contract fixtures
summary: Build shared fixture sets and automated contract checks that keep OpenAPI, domain semantics, SQLite migrations, and generated frontend bindings aligned.
objective: Make contract acceptance observable before the two implementation lanes run concurrently.
context: The accepted plan requires shared contracts and deterministic fixtures to be complete before parallel frontend/backend execution.
outputs: Sanitized JSON fixtures for profile, sources, refresh states, feed pages, article permissions, library state, and ranking explanations
RSS/Atom, official-API-shaped, and approved-scraper-shaped ingestion fixtures with no live credentials
Contract verification command covering schema validation, generated-client drift, fixture decoding, and migration application
Shared contract handoff document for the backend and frontend lanes
implementation_notes: Use fictional or permissively reusable fixture content and clearly mark permission mode.
Include both positive and negative fixtures, especially secrets, restricted content, invalid weights, and partial refresh failure.
Make fixture timestamps and identifiers deterministic.
Do not contact live providers in contract verification.
acceptance_criteria: One documented command validates OpenAPI, regenerates/checks frontend bindings, decodes all fixtures, and applies migrations to a temporary database.
Fixtures cover every API response family and each ingestion adapter shape planned for the MVP.
Negative fixtures prove secret values and unauthorized full content are rejected or omitted.
Backend and frontend implementers can consume the fixtures without editing shared contract files.
The independent reviewer records an explicit approval of the shared contract boundary before parallel lanes begin.
verification: Run the shared contract verification command from a clean checkout.
Run `git diff --exit-code` after generated binding checks.
Validate negative fixtures fail for the documented reason.
Have the independent reviewer compare fixture coverage with the merged project specification.
edge_cases: Absent optional profile and article fields
Partial refresh with both successes and failures
Generated client changes after only formatting differences
handoff_notes: This task is the explicit gate: dependent frontend and backend tasks may proceed in parallel only after its contract checks and reviewer approval pass.

title: Implement SQLite migrations and repositories
summary: Implement the migration runner, connection lifecycle, transactions, and repositories for all authoritative MVP records.
objective: Make profile, sources, articles, refresh runs, ranking state, and library state durable and queryable across restarts.
context: The accepted migration set is the only schema authority, SQLite is local and authoritative, and API secret values must never enter the database.
implementation_notes: Enable and verify foreign keys for every connection.
Use bounded connection settings appropriate for one local process and document journal/busy-timeout choices.
Map storage errors to domain/application errors without leaking SQL details through the API.
Keep credential identifiers separate from credential values.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh database migrates automatically and an existing current database opens without destructive changes.
Repository round trips preserve optional values, timestamps, permission mode, ranking components, and library state.
Refresh writes can commit successful source results while recording per-source failures according to application transaction boundaries.
Concurrent reads and serialized writes return predictable busy/cancellation errors rather than corrupting state.
No schema or repository method accepts API secret values.
verification: Run repository integration tests against temporary SQLite files.
Test migration from empty, current, interrupted, and unsupported-newer schema states.
Test unique, foreign-key, transaction rollback, cancellation, and restart persistence behavior.
Search database fixtures and schema for credential values.
edge_cases: Deleted source with retained library history
handoff_notes: Document transaction boundaries and query primitives used by ingestion and ranked-feed tasks.

title: Implement the Windows credential-store adapter
summary: Implement the credential-store port with Windows Credential Manager and a non-secret test double for other build environments.
objective: Allow optional official API adapters to use credentials without plaintext persistence, logging, or API disclosure.
context: Windows 11 is the MVP target, but Linux-based development and CI must still compile or test through build-tagged adapters and fakes.
implementation_notes: Use a stable application namespace and opaque credential reference derived from source identity.
Never return secret bytes through domain views or HTTP responses.
Zero or discard in-memory buffers when practical and avoid formatting secrets into errors.
Do not silently fall back to plaintext storage on unsupported platforms.
acceptance_criteria: On Windows, credentials can be written, resolved for adapter use, replaced, and deleted through the port.
Application-facing reads expose only configured state; only trusted adapter execution can resolve secret material.
Unsupported-platform behavior is explicit and tests can run without a real credential vault.
Logs, errors, API fixtures, SQLite, and snapshots contain no supplied secret values.
Deleting a source can follow a documented credential cleanup path without deleting unrelated entries.
verification: Run portable unit tests with sentinel secrets and assert redaction across errors/log capture.
Run Windows integration tests for create, replace, resolve-for-use, and delete.
Build on Windows and the primary non-Windows CI environment.
Search test artifacts and temporary SQLite files for sentinel secrets.
handoff_notes: Official API adapters receive a narrow resolve-for-use capability; HTTP handlers must never receive returned secret values.

title: Configure the Vue TypeScript PWA and generated API client
summary: Complete the Vue 3, TypeScript, Vite, and PWA setup and wire deterministic TypeScript client/type generation from the canonical OpenAPI contract.
objective: Provide an installable, buildable frontend boundary that cannot silently drift from the Go API.
context: The compiled SPA is embedded in the Go executable. Authoritative data remains behind the local API, and generated API files are never hand-edited.
implementation_notes: Choose a minimal state and routing setup supported by the accepted Vue stack; do not add alternative UI frameworks without need.
Scope service-worker caching to static application assets and explicitly safe GET responses; never cache credential mutations or secret-bearing requests.
Use same-origin relative `/api/v1` URLs so the embedded app talks only to its local host.
Keep generated bindings in the planned generated directory and regenerate them through one pinned command.
acceptance_criteria: The frontend passes lint, type checking, unit-test startup, and a production build from a clean checkout.
The generated client covers every canonical MVP endpoint and a drift check fails after an incompatible OpenAPI edit.
The production output lands in the exact location consumed by the Go embed build.
The manifest has stable application identity, install metadata, icons, display mode, and localhost-compatible start behavior.
Offline caching excludes credential operations and does not present stale mutation success as authoritative.
verification: Run frontend install, lint, typecheck, unit test, and production build commands.
Run API generation followed by a clean-tree drift assertion.
Run a manifest/service-worker configuration test for installability and cache exclusions.
Build the Go executable with the generated frontend assets.
edge_cases: App served on a non-default loopback port
handoff_notes: All later frontend work imports generated types through one wrapper module and treats service responses as authoritative.

title: Implement article normalization and deduplication
summary: Convert adapter records into canonical articles, normalize identifiers and metadata, enforce content permissions, and resolve duplicates deterministically.
objective: Ensure every source type writes consistent, rights-aware article records before ranking or presentation.
context: Different feeds may omit fields, republish the same story, or provide content that cannot be retained in full.
implementation_notes: Keep canonicalization conservative: never merge solely on a fuzzy title match.
Use source item identifiers when stable, canonical URLs when valid, and a documented fallback fingerprint.
Sanitize permitted HTML before storage or persist a safe normalized representation.
Metadata-only mode must discard supplied full bodies while retaining allowed title, excerpt, and publisher link.
acceptance_criteria: Equivalent repeated items update one article instead of creating duplicates.
Distinct articles with similar titles remain separate unless a stable identity rule matches.
Missing authors, dates, excerpts, or language values are handled without fabricating data.
Full content is retained only for sources whose recorded permission mode allows it and is sanitized before later rendering.
Normalization produces stable results for identical input fixtures.
verification: Run table-driven normalization and canonical-URL tests.
Run temporary-SQLite integration tests for insert, repeat, update, and collision cases.
Run sanitizer tests with malicious markup and metadata-only bodies.
Run deterministic fixture snapshots with fixed clock and identifiers.
handoff_notes: All adapters return neutral items to this service; they must not write article rows directly.

title: Implement profile and source-management services
summary: Implement application use cases for the single local profile, bounded ranking settings, starter/custom sources, scraper policy metadata, and credential lifecycle commands.
objective: Provide validated local configuration before ingestion and ranking features consume it.
context: Demographics are explicit, optional, disableable, and capped; location is manually selected; starter sources remain editable; scrapers require an approved policy record.
outputs: Source CRUD and starter-catalog import use cases
implementation_notes: Use one stable profile identity and idempotent first-run initialization.
Validate URL scheme, adapter kind, permission mode, and scraper policy metadata before enabling a source.
Enforce configured low-weight ceilings for demographic signals at the application boundary.
Keep the starter catalog data-driven and editable without recompiling application logic.
acceptance_criteria: Profile updates preserve absence versus disabled state and reject inferred or out-of-range demographic/ranking values.
Location accepts manual country/region and optional city without invoking geolocation or IP services.
Source CRUD supports starter and custom RSS/API/scraper records with type-specific validation.
A scraper cannot be enabled without explicit policy-review metadata and allowed content mode.
Credential commands store/delete secrets through the vault while database records retain only references/configured state.
verification: Run table-driven unit tests for profile, weights, source types, URLs, permission modes, and scraper policy validation.
Run integration tests proving profile/source state survives restart.
Run credential lifecycle tests with a fake vault and sentinel-secret leak assertions.
Test idempotent starter-catalog import and user edits.
edge_cases: Starter source edited then catalog reloaded
Credential write succeeds but database update fails
non_goals: Choosing final live source catalog entries
handoff_notes: Ingestion tasks consume only enabled, validated sources; ranking tasks consume the normalized bounded configuration.

title: Build the accessible application shell and routing
summary: Implement the responsive application frame, navigation, route structure, install affordance, loading boundaries, and global error presentation.
objective: Give every MVP workflow a consistent keyboard-accessible shell suitable for a Windows desktop browser or installed PWA window.
context: The accepted screens are first-run setup, ranked feed, article reader, personal library, sources/refresh, and profile/ranking settings.
implementation_notes: Use semantic landmarks, visible focus, keyboard navigation, and reduced-motion preferences from the start.
Do not hide local-server failures behind infinite loaders; show actionable retry/relaunch guidance.
Keep navigation usable in both browser tab and standalone PWA display modes.
Use route placeholders only as structural boundaries, not fake completed features.
acceptance_criteria: Each accepted MVP screen has a stable route and navigation entry or contextual path.
The shell works at common desktop widths and a narrow responsive viewport without horizontal navigation loss.
All navigation and global actions are keyboard operable with meaningful accessible names and visible focus.
Unknown routes, local API unavailability, recoverable errors, and PWA update availability have explicit states.
The shell does not store authoritative profile, article, source, ranking, or library data in browser storage.
verification: Run component tests for route navigation, not-found, loading, API-down, install, and update states.
Run automated accessibility checks on the shell and navigation.
Run keyboard-only navigation checks in the browser test runner.
Capture desktop and narrow-viewport screenshots.
handoff_notes: Feature screens should reuse shell status and error boundaries instead of implementing global behavior independently.

title: Implement the typed API and server-state layer
summary: Create the frontend API wrapper, query/mutation state, cancellation, polling, validation-error mapping, and safe cache policy around generated bindings.
objective: Give feature screens a consistent, testable route to authoritative backend state without duplicating domain or ranking rules.
context: The app is same-origin and local, but still needs robust startup, refresh polling, retries, mutation invalidation, and contract error handling.
implementation_notes: Choose one modest server-state mechanism and avoid parallel ad hoc fetch stores.
Cancel obsolete requests on route/query changes and stop polling on terminal refresh state or component disposal.
Never log request bodies from credential endpoints or persist their inputs.
Keep client-side optimistic state limited to reversible UI feedback; reconcile with mutation responses.
acceptance_criteria: Feature code consumes typed wrapper functions rather than raw fetch calls or handwritten response shapes.
Queries and mutations have explicit loading, empty, success, validation, conflict, unavailable, and unexpected-error behavior.
Refresh polling stops on success, partial success, failure, cancellation, timeout, or unmount.
Successful mutations invalidate only relevant server state and use returned authoritative values.
Credential values are absent from caches, logs, persisted stores, error messages, and test snapshots.
verification: Run unit tests with generated-contract fixtures for every error family and mutation invalidation rule.
Run fake-timer tests for polling lifecycle and cancellation.
Run a sentinel-secret test across logger, cache serialization, and snapshots.
Run TypeScript and generated-client drift checks.
edge_cases: Network failure after server committed mutation
handoff_notes: Document query keys and mutation invalidations so independently developed screens do not create conflicting caches.

title: Implement deterministic local text similarity
summary: Implement local tokenization, indexing, and TF-IDF/BM25-style similarity behind the accepted ranking port.
objective: Provide lightweight content-interest matching without external AI services, model runtimes, or network calls.
context: The MVP chose replaceable lightweight local text similarity. Results must be deterministic, explainable, restart-safe, and suitable for one user's local corpus.
implementation_notes: Normalize case and Unicode predictably and document language limitations rather than inferring unsupported language semantics.
Use title and allowed excerpt/content fields with explicit field weighting; never fetch extra content for ranking.
Version tokenization and similarity parameters so stored results can be invalidated safely.
Keep the interface replaceable for a postponed embedding implementation.
acceptance_criteria: Identical corpus, profile interests, configuration, clock, and algorithm version produce identical scores.
The scorer handles empty interests, empty text, small corpora, common terms, Unicode, and repeated tokens without invalid numeric results.
Index state can be rebuilt solely from permitted locally stored article fields.
Similarity produces a bounded normalized contribution and machine-readable matching terms/reasons.
No runtime network request, external AI service, embedding model, or separate model process is used.
verification: Run golden ranking fixtures for tokenization, corpus statistics, and score ordering.
Run determinism tests across repeated builds and database reloads.
Run property/fuzz tests for finite bounded scores and malformed Unicode input.
Run a test proving the scorer has no outbound-network dependency.
handoff_notes: Expose contribution details, not UI prose; the combined scorer owns final explanation ordering.

title: Expose profile and source APIs
summary: Implement contract-compliant HTTP handlers for health/readiness, profile, ranking configuration, starter sources, source CRUD, and write/delete-only credentials.
objective: Complete the backend platform API slice needed by first-run and source-management frontend work.
context: Handlers must follow the accepted OpenAPI contract, remain thin over application services, and prevent secret or internal error leakage.
outputs: Consistent validation/error middleware and contract tests
implementation_notes: Decode with bounded body sizes and reject unknown fields where the contract is closed.
Return stable error codes and correlation identifiers without stack traces or secret-bearing causes.
Apply request timeouts and cancellation to application calls.
Do not add authentication as a substitute for the required loopback binding.
acceptance_criteria: Implemented operations match canonical paths, methods, status codes, and schemas.
Invalid optional demographics, weights, source settings, and policy metadata produce stable validation errors.
Credential endpoints accept write/delete operations but never return stored secret values.
Handlers map not-found, conflict, unsupported-platform, and internal failures without leaking implementation details.
All endpoints are reachable through the composed loopback server and API 404 behavior remains isolated from SPA fallback.
verification: Run handler unit tests for success and every documented error family.
Run OpenAPI response/request conformance tests using shared fixtures.
Run loopback integration tests through a temporary SQLite database and fake credential store.
Run sentinel-secret scans over responses and captured logs.
non_goals: Refresh, feed, article, and library handlers
handoff_notes: Frontend first-run/source tasks may integrate after these conformance tests and the independent review gate pass.

title: Implement bounded and policy-aware HTTP fetching
summary: Implement the shared outbound fetcher with timeouts, size limits, redirect controls, rate limiting, safe URL validation, and sanitized diagnostics.
objective: Give all network ingestion adapters one enforceable safety boundary before they contact public sources.
context: RSS, official APIs, and approved scrapers share outbound-network risks. Local-only use does not permit access-control, robots, rate-limit, or publisher-policy bypass.
implementation_notes: Reject non-HTTP(S) URLs, embedded credentials, loopback/private/link-local destinations reached directly or through redirects, and unsupported redirects.
Enforce response byte limits before buffering and allow per-adapter content-type allowlists.
Use a descriptive User-Agent, conditional request headers, and bounded retry behavior that honors Retry-After.
Do not log authorization headers, query secrets, response bodies, or credential-bearing URLs.
acceptance_criteria: Every ingestion adapter can fetch only through the shared bounded fetcher.
Timeouts, redirects, DNS/address validation, response limits, content types, conditional requests, and per-source pacing are configurable within safe caps.
Private-network and redirect-to-private-network attempts are rejected before content is returned.
429 and transient failures produce bounded retry metadata without bypassing provider limits.
Errors and logs contain source-safe context but no secrets or response content.
verification: Run unit tests with a controlled HTTP server for timeout, redirect, size, type, ETag, Last-Modified, 429, and cancellation behavior.
Run negative tests for loopback/private/link-local targets and redirect chains.
Run sentinel-secret checks across errors and captured logs.
Run race-enabled tests where supported.
edge_cases: DNS rebinding between validation and connection
handoff_notes: RSS, API, and scraper adapters must not instantiate independent unrestricted HTTP clients.

title: Create shared accessible UI primitives and test fixtures
summary: Implement reusable form, status, article-summary, ranking-explanation, filtering, confirmation, and empty-state components backed by contract fixtures.
objective: Prevent feature screens from duplicating sensitive controls, permission messaging, and interaction behavior.
context: Optional demographics, credential writes, scraper policy state, article permissions, refresh failures, and ranking reasons need consistent explicit presentation.
implementation_notes: Demographic fields must state that they are optional, local, low-weight, and individually disableable.
Credential inputs are write-only and must clear from component memory after submission or cancellation.
Do not render full-content HTML in summary components; reader sanitization belongs to the feature workflow.
Use stable reason codes from the API and provide an explicit fallback for unknown future codes.
acceptance_criteria: Shared components cover all repeated interaction and status patterns required by the four workflow tasks.
Labels, descriptions, validation messages, keyboard behavior, focus movement, and live-region announcements are accessible.
Article components distinguish full-content-allowed from metadata-only and always preserve the canonical publisher link.
Ranking explanations reflect API contributions without recomputing or exaggerating causal meaning.
Credential inputs never retain submitted values in global state, browser persistence, logs, or snapshots.
verification: Run component tests across default, loading, empty, error, disabled, and success variants.
Run automated accessibility checks and keyboard interaction tests.
Run malicious-content and unknown-reason fixtures.
Run sentinel-secret lifecycle and snapshot checks for credential controls.
edge_cases: Very long title or source name
handoff_notes: Workflow tasks should compose these primitives and add new shared behavior only with focused component tests.

title: Implement primary ranking signal extractors
summary: Compute bounded recency, explicit-interest, source-preference, library-feedback, and coarse-location contributions independently of final score aggregation.
objective: Make each primary personalization signal testable and explainable before weights combine them.
context: Explicit interests, selected sources, recency, and reading actions must lead ranking; coarse manually entered location may contribute without automatic geolocation.
implementation_notes: Use an injected clock and explicit decay parameters for recency.
Treat hidden state as feed exclusion, not an arbitrarily large negative score.
Define reading-action effects conservatively so a single action cannot permanently dominate the feed.
Location matching uses only explicit coarse profile/source/article metadata and never infers physical location.
acceptance_criteria: Each signal returns a finite documented range plus stable explanation data.
Empty or disabled signals contribute zero and do not fabricate evidence.
Recency behavior is deterministic under a fixed clock and handles missing/future timestamps safely.
Source and reading-action signals distinguish explicit preference from incidental availability.
Location uses manually selected country/region and optional city only.
verification: Run table-driven tests for every signal at minimum, maximum, absent, disabled, and malformed-input boundaries.
Run fixed-clock recency tests including future and missing publication times.
Run behavior tests for read, saved, hidden, restored, and untouched articles.
Run coarse-location matching tests without geolocation or IP calls.
handoff_notes: The combined scorer may weight these contributions but must not duplicate or mutate their extraction rules.

title: Implement RSS and Atom ingestion
summary: Implement the feed adapter for RSS and Atom variants using the bounded fetcher and normalization pipeline.
objective: Deliver the baseline source type that can populate the MVP without API credentials or scraping.
context: Feeds vary in date formats, namespaces, identifiers, relative links, summaries, and whether full content is supplied.
implementation_notes: Support common RSS 2.0 and Atom forms without relying on browser HTML repair.
Resolve relative links against the final allowed response URL.
Map feed content into the neutral adapter item and let normalization enforce retention permission.
A malformed item should be skipped with diagnostics when the rest of the feed remains usable.
acceptance_criteria: Representative RSS and Atom fixtures produce normalized articles with stable identity and metadata.
ETag and Last-Modified values are persisted and a not-modified response performs no article writes.
Malformed feeds fail safely; isolated malformed items do not necessarily discard valid siblings.
Relative links, namespaces, date variants, encodings, summaries, and full-content elements follow documented mappings.
The adapter cannot bypass fetcher limits or content permission enforcement.
verification: Run parser tests across the shared RSS/Atom fixture corpus.
Run controlled-server tests for conditional requests and not-modified responses.
Run partial-item failure and malformed-document tests.
Run an end-to-end adapter-to-temporary-SQLite test.
non_goals: Choosing the final starter feed catalog
handoff_notes: Provider-specific quirks belong in fixtures or narrowly scoped normalization rules, not source-name conditionals in the core domain.

title: Implement official API and approved scraper adapter foundations
summary: Create configurable fixture-backed adapter foundations for one official JSON API shape and one allowlisted public-page scraper shape without selecting or contacting a live provider.
objective: Prove the planned adapter boundaries, credentials, policy metadata, and permission enforcement while preserving unresolved provider choices.
context: The merged intake accepts official APIs and narrowly approved scrapers, but the first live providers and targets remain intentionally unresolved.
inputs: Validated source and scraper policy records
implementation_notes: Do not embed a real provider hostname, key, or production scraper selector until a later accepted task names and reviews that target.
API credentials must be attached only at request time and never copied into source configuration or diagnostics.
Scraper activation requires explicit allowlist/policy metadata and a stored robots review result; runtime must fail closed when metadata is absent or stale under the accepted policy.
Selectors extract only fields allowed by the recorded permission mode.
acceptance_criteria: A fictional official API fixture demonstrates pagination/cursor mapping, rate-limit metadata, credential use, and neutral-item output.
A fictional permitted public-page fixture demonstrates selector extraction, canonical URL handling, and metadata-only/full-content permission enforcement.
The scraper refuses execution without approved policy metadata and cannot request login/paywall/access-control bypass behavior.
Neither adapter stores, logs, returns, or fixtures a secret value.
Adding a future provider is isolated to a new configuration/adapter and tests rather than changes to core ingestion logic.
verification: Run fixture-backed API pagination, 401/403, 429, invalid-shape, and cancellation tests.
Run fixture-backed scraper selector, robots/policy refusal, malicious markup, and permission tests.
Run sentinel-secret scans across logs, errors, fixtures, and temporary SQLite files.
Run a test proving no live network request is made by the fixture suite.
proof_required: Statement that no live provider was selected
edge_cases: Page redirects to a disallowed host
handoff_notes: A later provider-specific task must name the source, confirm terms/robots/rate limits/content rights, add fixtures, and receive independent review.

title: Implement first-run setup and profile settings
summary: Build the guided first-run and editable profile/ranking-settings screens for interests, starter sources, coarse location, optional demographics, and bounded signal controls.
objective: Let the user establish transparent local personalization without an account, automatic location, or inferred demographic values.
context: Explicit interests and source choices lead ranking. Country/region is manual; city, age, and gender are optional, local, disableable, and low-weight.
implementation_notes: Determine first-run state from authoritative API data, not a browser-local completed flag.
Present demographic fields after primary preferences and explain their optional, local, capped effect before entry.
Use separate enabled controls so clearing a value and disabling its ranking effect are understandable.
Do not request browser geolocation or perform IP-based location lookup.
acceptance_criteria: A new user can choose starter sources, enter interests, select country/region, optionally add city/age/gender, review signal controls, and save a valid local profile.
Age, gender, and city can be omitted; age/gender can be individually disabled and their capped influence is visible.
Invalid weights, locations, or profile fields show field-level contract errors without discarding valid unsaved entries.
Returning users bypass first-run setup and can edit or clear every accepted profile value.
No profile value is sent outside the same-origin local API or persisted as authoritative browser state.
verification: Run component tests for new, partial, valid, invalid, saved, and API-error states.
Run accessibility and keyboard tests for all fields, enable controls, validation summaries, and save feedback.
Run a browser test from empty profile through completed setup and reload.
Assert no browser geolocation/IP request and no authoritative profile persistence in browser storage.
handoff_notes: Feed ranking explanations must reflect the server's saved configuration rather than unsaved form state.

title: Combine scores with demographic caps and explanations
summary: Implement normalized weighted aggregation, optional low-weight age/gender adjustments, deterministic ordering, and persisted ranking explanations.
objective: Produce the final relevance order while enforcing the accepted transparency, privacy, and demographic-subordination policy.
context: Demographics may make only small optional adjustments. Primary signals and text similarity lead, and every article must explain its placement.
implementation_notes: Normalize configured weights and reject invalid, negative, non-finite, or all-zero active configurations according to the domain contract.
Enforce hard aggregate and per-signal caps for age/gender regardless of configured input.
Use stable tie-breakers such as score, publication time, then article identifier.
Build explanations from actual nonzero contributions and stable reason codes; do not claim causal facts not present in inputs.
acceptance_criteria: Final scores are finite, bounded, deterministic, and accompanied by contributions that reconcile to the documented total.
Disabling or omitting age/gender produces exactly zero contribution and no demographic explanation.
Enabled demographic contributions cannot exceed accepted low-weight caps or outrank the aggregate primary-signal budget by themselves.
Tie ordering is stable across recomputation and restart.
Every visible result has at least one truthful explanation or an explicit neutral/default reason.
verification: Run golden end-to-end ranking fixtures with contribution reconciliation.
Run property tests for finite bounds, deterministic order, and demographic caps across generated configurations.
Run metamorphic tests showing disabled demographics cannot change order or explanations.
Run persistence/reload tests for algorithm version and components.
non_goals: Automated weight tuning from multiple users
handoff_notes: Expose stable contribution/reason structures through the API; the frontend may localize wording but must not change meaning.

title: Implement refresh orchestration and status API
summary: Coordinate bounded manual refresh runs across enabled sources, persist per-source outcomes, isolate failures, and expose contract-compliant refresh start/status endpoints.
objective: Turn the ingestion adapters into an observable user-triggered pipeline that updates articles safely while the app is running.
context: The MVP supports manual refresh and refresh-while-running only. One bad source must not discard successful work from others.
outputs: POST refresh and GET refresh-status handlers
implementation_notes: Permit at most one active global refresh unless the contract explicitly defines source-scoped concurrency.
Bound source concurrency and propagate process/request cancellation without leaving a run permanently marked active.
Commit successful source results independently where the accepted transaction design permits.
Sanitize all user-facing errors and retain only bounded diagnostic summaries.
acceptance_criteria: Starting a refresh returns a stable run identifier and status progresses through running to success, partial success, failure, or cancelled.
A concurrent start request receives the contract-defined conflict behavior rather than launching duplicate work.
One source failure is recorded without rolling back successful source ingestion.
Per-source fetched/inserted/updated/skipped/failed counts and sanitized messages persist across restart.
Shutdown or cancellation leaves a terminal, recoverable RefreshRun state.
verification: Run integration tests with mixed successful, unchanged, malformed, rate-limited, and failed fixture sources.
Test concurrent refresh conflict, bounded concurrency, cancellation, shutdown, and restart status retrieval.
Validate refresh endpoints against OpenAPI fixtures.
Run race-enabled coordinator tests where supported.
non_goals: Ingestion while the executable is closed
handoff_notes: Ranking recomputation consumes committed article changes and must not block persistence of refresh outcomes.

title: Implement source management and manual refresh
summary: Build source catalog/custom-source management, write-only credential controls, scraper policy visibility, refresh initiation, polling, and per-source outcome presentation.
objective: Let the user safely control what is ingested and understand refresh progress and failures without exposing secrets.
context: The MVP includes editable starter sources, manual RSS/API/approved-scraper configuration, and ingestion only while the executable runs.
implementation_notes: Show adapter type, enabled state, permission mode, credential configured state, and scraper policy status without displaying credential content.
Clear credential inputs immediately after successful submission, cancellation, route change, or component disposal.
Explain that refresh runs only while the app process is open.
Differentiate success, unchanged, partial success, failure, cancelled, conflict, and rate-limited outcomes.
acceptance_criteria: The user can enable/edit starter entries and add validated custom RSS, official API, or approved scraper source configurations.
Scraper configuration cannot appear enabled without required policy status and permission information from the API.
Credential UI supports configure/replace/delete and displays only configured/not-configured state.
One manual refresh can be started, duplicate-start conflict is explained, and polling stops at a terminal state.
Per-source counts and sanitized failures remain understandable after navigation or reload.
verification: Run component tests for every source kind, validation family, credential lifecycle, and deletion confirmation.
Run fake-timer tests for refresh polling and component disposal.
Run browser coverage from source creation through mixed-outcome refresh.
Run sentinel-secret checks across DOM, logs, caches, snapshots, and browser storage.
handoff_notes: Integration tests should use fictional fixtures; live provider setup remains an explicit later selection.

title: Implement ranked feed and article query APIs
summary: Implement paginated ranked-feed and article-detail queries with basic filters, permission-aware content, and contract-compliant explanations.
objective: Expose the local ranked corpus to the PWA without duplicating ranking logic or leaking unauthorized content.
context: The feed must support read/unread, saved, hidden, source, and basic search/filter behavior while SQLite remains authoritative.
implementation_notes: Default feed excludes hidden articles and returns current persisted rank order.
Use stable cursor/page keys that cannot duplicate or omit unchanged rows across adjacent pages.
Return sanitized full content only in full-content-allowed mode; otherwise return metadata/excerpt and canonical publisher URL.
Basic text filtering operates locally over permitted stored fields.
acceptance_criteria: Feed results follow deterministic rank order with stable pagination and include machine-readable explanation components.
Filters cover source, read/unread, saved, hidden visibility, and accepted basic text/date behavior.
Article detail never returns stored or derived full content for metadata-only sources.
Unknown or malformed cursors/identifiers produce contract-defined errors.
Queries remain bounded and use the planned SQLite indexes for representative local data volumes.
verification: Run API conformance tests for feed and article endpoints.
Run pagination tests for empty, single-page, multi-page, ties, and filtered datasets.
Run content-permission negative tests and malicious-content rendering fixtures.
Inspect representative query plans and run bounded performance checks on generated local data.
edge_cases: Metadata-only article with accidentally populated body
handoff_notes: Frontend feed/reader work must consume returned rank and permission state without recreating backend rules.

title: Implement library actions and ranking recomputation
summary: Implement persistent read, saved, and hidden mutations plus targeted ranking recomputation after ingestion, profile, configuration, or library changes.
objective: Complete the feedback loop and preserve user state and rank behavior across restarts.
context: Library actions are both user-visible state and bounded ranking inputs. Recalculation must not block successful ingestion indefinitely or produce stale explanations.
implementation_notes: Model read, saved, and hidden as independently reversible timestamps/states.
Serialize or version recomputation so an older run cannot overwrite results calculated from newer inputs.
Prefer targeted recomputation when one article/library state changes and bounded full recomputation when corpus/configuration changes.
Hidden state excludes the article by default but restoring it must make the article eligible again.
acceptance_criteria: Read/unread, save/unsave, and hide/restore operations are idempotent and persist across restart.
Library mutations return the contract-defined current state and trigger only the documented ranking updates.
Article ingestion, profile changes, ranking-config changes, and algorithm-version changes result in fresh compatible RankingResults.
Concurrent or cancelled recomputation cannot commit stale results over newer input versions.
A recomputation failure preserves readable prior data, reports sanitized status, and remains retryable.
verification: Run table-driven state-transition tests for every action and reversal.
Run API conformance and restart-persistence tests.
Run concurrency tests for overlapping mutations, refresh completion, and configuration changes.
Run stale-version, cancellation, retry, and partial-failure recomputation tests.
handoff_notes: Frontend workflows may treat successful mutation responses as authoritative and then refresh affected feed queries.

title: Implement the ranked feed and permission-aware reader
summary: Build the primary feed with pagination, filters, ranking explanations, article actions, refresh affordance, and an article reader that respects content permission mode.
objective: Deliver the core daily-use experience: see relevant news first, understand why, and read permitted content or open the publisher.
context: The backend owns score order and explanations. Hidden articles are excluded by default, and metadata-only articles must link out rather than render extracted full text.
implementation_notes: Preserve server order and display returned reason components without client-side score calculation.
Make publisher, publication time, permission mode, and outbound destination clear before navigation.
Render permitted content only through a reviewed sanitization boundary and block active markup/script execution.
Use mutation responses as authoritative and recover cleanly when optimistic interaction conflicts with server state.
acceptance_criteria: The default feed shows server-ranked non-hidden articles with stable pagination, source/date metadata, and concise truthful reasons.
The user can filter by source, read/unread, saved state, and accepted basic text/date options and can clear filters.
Read, save, and hide actions update visibly, survive query refresh, and expose accessible success/failure feedback.
Full-content-allowed articles render sanitized content; metadata-only articles never render a body and always provide the canonical publisher link.
Empty, initial loading, additional-page loading, stale/retry, partial-refresh, and API-unavailable states are distinct.
verification: Run component tests for feed ordering, filters, pagination, explanations, actions, and all status states.
Run malicious permitted-content fixtures through the reader and assert active content cannot execute.
Run browser coverage from refresh result to feed, explanation, reader/link-out, and inline actions.
Run accessibility tests for article lists, explanation disclosure, filters, and reader focus.
handoff_notes: The end-to-end acceptance flow should exercise this screen with persisted fixture data and a real local backend.

title: Review layered CI and contract verification
summary: Independently verify that repository automation exercises Go, frontend, OpenAPI, generated bindings, migrations, fixtures, and cross-stack integration with enforceable failures.
objective: Confirm every implementation PR has repeatable baseline evidence before product-level acceptance testing.
context: The reviewer is an independent mandatory gate and must reject missing, bypassed, flaky, or non-enforcing checks.
allowed_areas: Read all repository files and PR diffs
implementation_notes: Review configuration and actual logs; a named check that skips relevant work is not proof.
Confirm generated-client drift and task-batch/lifecycle checks fail the build when inconsistent.
Do not repair production implementation while acting as its reviewer.
Treat unexplained skipped tests, ignored failures, or mutable unpinned generation as blocking.
acceptance_criteria: Go formatting/static analysis/tests, frontend lint/typecheck/tests/build, OpenAPI validation, generated-client drift, migration tests, and integration tests run in documented automation.
Required checks return nonzero on seeded representative failures and do not silently skip due to missing prerequisites.
Test artifacts and logs contain no secrets, private profile payloads, or unpermitted article content.
The reviewer records APPROVE only when evidence is reproducible; otherwise the task ends REJECTED with corrections.
verification: Re-run documented verification from a clean checkout.
Inspect CI triggers, permissions, caching, failure propagation, and Windows coverage.
Perform controlled negative checks for contract drift and failing tests.
Compare covered commands with each task's proof requirements.
edge_cases: Test command succeeds with zero tests
non_goals: Approving product behavior before end-to-end checks
handoff_notes: A REJECT decision blocks final acceptance until implementers supply corrected automation and new evidence.

title: Implement personal library and settings integration
summary: Build saved/read/hidden library views, reversible state management, persistent filters, and cohesive links among library, profile, ranking, sources, and feed settings.
objective: Complete the persistent personal reading workflow and make all user-controlled ranking inputs discoverable and reversible.
context: The user selected read/unread, save-for-later, hide/dismiss, and basic filtering as MVP features. SQLite is authoritative across restarts.
implementation_notes: Store only disposable view/filter preferences in browser storage; retrieve all article/library state from the API.
Make hidden items intentionally discoverable in a management view so hide remains reversible.
Keep filter URL/query state understandable for back/forward navigation where practical.
After profile or ranking changes, show backend recomputation progress/stale state if the contract exposes it.
acceptance_criteria: Saved, read/unread, and hidden views load authoritative state and allow the accepted reversible actions.
Library state and server-backed filters survive application restart; disposable UI preferences may survive browser reload without becoming authoritative.
Restoring a hidden article makes it eligible for normal feed display after authoritative refresh.
Settings navigation clearly separates profile, ranking signals, sources, credentials, and refresh information.
The complete workflow remains usable by keyboard and presents useful empty/error states for each library view.
verification: Run component tests for saved, read/unread, hidden/restore, filters, reload, and error states.
Run browser coverage that changes actions, restarts/reloads the app, and confirms SQLite-backed persistence.
Inspect browser storage to confirm it contains no authoritative library records, profile data, article content, or credentials.
Run accessibility checks and keyboard-only action reversal.
edge_cases: Article state changes from another open tab
handoff_notes: Integration-release must prove the complete daily-use workflow across a real process restart, not only a browser reload.

title: Verify the complete daily-use browser workflow
summary: Independently run the critical path from first launch through setup, source refresh, ranked reading, library actions, and process restart persistence.
objective: Prove the assembled product satisfies the accepted daily-use MVP rather than only isolated component contracts.
context: The selected acceptance threshold requires installation/launch, profile and sources, refresh, explainable ranking, permission-aware reading, filtering, and persistent state.
allowed_areas: Read all repository files and PR diffs
Review notes, screenshots, traces, and verification reports
implementation_notes: Exercise the real Go process, SQLite database, served Vue build, and API rather than mocking the backend.
Use fictional/permitted deterministic source fixtures, not live provider availability, for the acceptance path.
Include keyboard interaction and at least one narrow viewport check even though Windows desktop is primary.
Restart means stop and relaunch the Go process, not merely reload the browser.
acceptance_criteria: A clean user-data directory reaches first-run setup and saves explicit interests, coarse location, optional/disabled demographics, and starter source choices.
Manual refresh ingests fixtures, reports mixed outcomes correctly, and produces a ranked feed with truthful reason components.
Permitted content renders safely in-app while metadata-only content shows no body and opens the canonical publisher URL.
Read/unread, saved, hidden/restored, and filters behave correctly and authoritative state survives full process restart.
The reviewer issues APPROVE only if the workflow and accessibility evidence meet requirements; otherwise issues REJECT with reproduced failures.
verification: Run the critical-path browser suite against a packaged-like local process and temporary SQLite database.
Repeat key assertions after stopping and relaunching the process.
Run automated accessibility checks plus keyboard-only navigation through the core path.
Inspect browser storage and outbound requests for privacy-boundary violations.
handoff_notes: Preserve deterministic artifacts so failures can be replayed by an implementer without access to reviewer-local state.

title: Verify Windows executable packaging and runtime boundaries
summary: Independently build and smoke-test the Windows executable, embedded PWA, loopback binding, browser launch, credential integration, migrations, and shutdown behavior.
objective: Prove the MVP can be used directly on Windows 11 with the promised single-executable launch model.
context: Windows behavior cannot be inferred solely from Linux cross-compilation, especially browser launch and Credential Manager integration.
allowed_areas: Read all repository files and PR diffs
Review notes, build logs, and smoke-test artifacts
inputs: Fresh and existing test data directories
implementation_notes: Require native Windows execution evidence in addition to any cross-build.
Test from a path containing spaces and without assuming administrator privileges.
Inspect listening sockets to prove no wildcard/LAN binding.
Use a sentinel API key and prove Credential Manager cleanup and absence from database/logs.
acceptance_criteria: A documented clean build produces the intended Windows executable with embedded frontend assets.
Launching without administrator privileges initializes/migrates local data, binds only to loopback, becomes ready, and opens the default browser once.
Credential create/use/replace/delete works through Windows Credential Manager and the sentinel value is absent from SQLite, logs, errors, and artifacts.
A second-instance or occupied-port case behaves according to documented safe behavior, and shutdown leaves no corrupt active refresh/migration state.
The reviewer records APPROVE only with native evidence; otherwise records REJECT and the exact failed boundary.
verification: Run the release build and checksum step.
Run native Windows startup, readiness, browser-open, embedded-route, socket-binding, and shutdown smoke tests.
Run fresh/current/unsupported-newer migration cases on Windows.
Run Windows Credential Manager lifecycle and sentinel-secret scans.
handoff_notes: Cross-compilation alone is insufficient; a native Windows run is required before approval.

title: Perform final privacy, policy, and MVP acceptance review
summary: Audit the complete implementation and evidence against merged requirements, safety boundaries, architecture, ownership rules, and every MVP acceptance signal.
objective: Issue the mandatory final reviewer decision that determines whether the MVP task set is acceptable for release consideration.
context: Reviewer rejection is binding. Unresolved blocking findings, missing proof, deferred-scope leakage, or unsafe source behavior prevent approval.
allowed_areas: Read all repository files, history, PR diffs, task runs, submissions, reviews, tests, artifacts, and generated lifecycle state
Review notes and final acceptance report
inputs: All implementation PRs and task-run proof
CI, browser, Windows, privacy, and policy evidence
outputs: Explicit final APPROVE or REJECT decision
implementation_notes: Trace every accepted must-have and safety boundary to implementation plus observable proof.
Inspect actual scraper/API configurations; fictional adapter foundations do not authorize an unreviewed live target.
Confirm postponed features did not enter the implementation through convenience additions.
Do not downgrade missing evidence to a non-blocking note when the task requires proof.
acceptance_criteria: Every MVP must-have and acceptance signal has implementation and passing evidence, or the review is REJECTED.

No external AI/profile processing, automatic geolocation, inferred demographics, plaintext credentials, unauthorized full content, prohibited scraping, non-loopback exposure, account/sync feature, or background-service scope is present.
All implementation PRs have an independent approved review with blocking findings resolved and no self-approval conflict.
The canonical backlog, collaboration state, task-run proof, and repository state agree on completion without stale or fabricated status.
The final decision is a single explicit APPROVE or REJECT with evidence-linked rationale.
verification: Run or inspect the full required verification suite and compare it with merged acceptance signals.
Perform repository-wide secret, private-data, prohibited-scope, network-binding, and content-permission audits.
Trace representative requirements through task, PR, code, test, and proof records.
Check dependency completion and reviewer independence in collaboration history.
edge_cases: A check passed on an older commit
Task marked done without accepted proof
Live source added after adapter review
non_goals: Accepting risks on the user's behalf
handoff_notes: Any REJECT decision returns work to the responsible implementation task/PR; only an explicit APPROVE satisfies the accepted review gate.
